_readme: WHAT A CHANNEL MEANS. Not where it is -- that is hardware/<box>.json, and the
split is the point: a box with a different pinout swaps that file and touches
nothing here, because everything downstream resolves channels by NAME and by
KIND and never by pin arithmetic.
`direction` is declared once per KIND rather than per channel. It is a function
of the kind -- engagement and response are inputs, emitters, rewards, cue and
vacuum are outputs -- and declaring it per channel made 'a reward line that is
`well` stays here even though it is a plumbing fact, because its VALUE is a
logical channel name and its job is to catch a reward line wired to the wrong
side of the box. A rig that re-plumbs which fluid line feeds which well edits
this file; see the note in the pinout.

engagement.doc: The port whose entry initiates a trial, and where the animal samples. EXACTLY ONE channel may carry this kind -- the trial runner resolves the engagement wait, the commitment hold, the sampling hold and the sampling release to it by kind rather than by name, which is what lets one sketch serve a box with a different port name.

response.doc: A port a trial type may name as its correct response.

emitter.doc: A stimulus actuator. 'Stimulus' is an emitter channel and nothing more, which is why a speaker or LED substitutes for an odor valve with no change to the trial runner.

reward.doc: A reward actuator. Pulse width is the delivered magnitude.

cue.doc: A trial-availability signal driven by entry actions, not a stimulus.

vacuum.doc: Odor-routing hardware with no behavioural meaning of its own.

odor_port.rationale: The engagement port. Named in no task profile because it is resolved by kind -- an engagement port is a structural fact of the box, not a per-task choice.

right_well.rationale: INPUT_PULLUP: LOW means the beam is broken, i.e. poked -- the polarity `verifySensor()` reads. `port_slot` names which family of per-port strobes this port reports with (strobe_vocab `port_slots`); slot 2 is the historical _R family, so the recorded archive is unchanged.

left_well.rationale: See right_well. Slot 1 is the historical _L family.

trial_light.rationale: Trial availability: raised when the trial opens, dropped on every path out of it. Named in no task profile for the same reason as odor_port. Its OFF edge pairs with a behavioural strobe and the order flips between paths -- LIGHTS_OFF follows ODOR_UNPOKE on a completed trial and follows LAZY_RAT on an abstention.

vacuum.rationale: Normally-open. Closed once the commitment hold is satisfied, which is what routes odor to the port; reopened when sampling ends. Purely mechanical -- it carries no strobe of its own.

odor_line_7.rationale: Odor solenoid 7. Note the pin ordering is NOT monotonic past line 6 -- 22,24,26,28,30,32 then 23,25,27,29,31,33 -- which is why channels resolve by name and never by arithmetic.

fluid_0.rationale: Left well, reward line 1. `well` is declared so a task profile that rewards the left well through a right-well line is refused -- a mistake that would look correct on screen and deliver water to the wrong side of the box.

fluid_1.rationale: Left well, reward line 2. Unused by every current task; present because the hardware has it.

fluid_3.rationale: Right well, reward line 2. Unused by every current task.
